name: Differential Privacy
description: Differentially private mechanisms, analytics, and deployments, including local DP.

ccs.narrative:
Differential privacy research at CCS has grown from foundational mechanism design to applied DP in ML and graph analytics. The 2018 cohort tackled a broad range of settings: Detecting Violations of Differential Privacy (CCS 2018) automated correctness testing for DP implementations, Utility-Aware Synthesis of Differentially Private and Attack-Resilient Location Traces (CCS 2018) addressed location privacy with utility constraints, and CALM: Consistent Adaptive Local Marginal for Marginal Release under Local Differential Privacy (CCS 2018) improved local DP for marginal query release.

Graph DP became a distinct sub-area starting in 2019: Analyzing Subgraph Statistics from Extended Local Views with Decentralized Differential Privacy (CCS 2019) applied decentralized DP to social graph analysis, and Locally Private Graph Neural Networks (CCS 2021) extended local DP to GNN training to protect node features. Private Summation in the Multi-Message Shuffle Model (CCS 2020) explored the shuffle model as an intermediate privacy tier between local and central DP.

From 2022, DP intersected with the LLM boom. DP-Forward: Fine-tuning and Inference on Language Models with Differential Privacy in Forward Pass (CCS 2023) introduced forward-pass perturbation to protect against embedding-level inference attacks during fine-tuning. Evaluations of Machine Learning Privacy Defenses are Misleading (CCS 2024) questioned the reliability of DP evaluation benchmarks, pointing toward methodological reform.

ndss.narrative:
Differential privacy at NDSS has been a focused but consistently technical thread, concerned with making DP mechanisms both practical and robust against adversaries who try to exploit the privacy guarantees. MBeacon (NDSS 2019) applied DP to genomic methylation beacons, an early example of the field grounding abstract theory in sensitive medical data. At the same time, Private Continual Release of Real-Valued Data Streams tackled the harder setting of ongoing publication.

Work in 2020 pushed DP into adversarial territory. Adversarial Classification Under Differential Privacy (NDSS 2020) studied how DP interacts with classification tasks when the adversary is aware of the mechanism, while Secure Sublinear Time Differentially Private Median Computation introduced efficient protocols for private statistics. Locally differentially private protocols (Locally Differentially Private Frequency Estimation with Consistency, NDSS 2020) addressed the setting where no trusted aggregator exists.

The 2022–2025 papers show two extensions: DP deployed in urban and mobile sensing pipelines (Privacy in Urban Sensing with Instrumented Fleets, NDSS 2022) and a refinement of local DP estimation theory (Revisiting EM-based Estimation for Locally Differentially Private Protocols, NDSS 2025). Throughout, the community has maintained a dual focus on formal guarantees and the practical overheads of achieving them in realistic deployments.

milestones.title: Secure Sublinear Time Differentially Private Median Computation
milestones.note: Computes the median over two parties' data in sublinear time with differential privacy and secure two-party computation.

milestones.title: Locally Differentially Private Frequency Estimation with Consistency
milestones.note: Improves locally differentially private frequency estimation by enforcing consistency constraints to boost accuracy.

milestones.title: Privacy in Urban Sensing with Instrumented Fleets, Using Air Pollution Monitoring As A Usecase
milestones.note: Designs privacy-preserving urban sensing for instrumented vehicle fleets, demonstrated on air-pollution monitoring.

milestones.title: Revisiting EM-based Estimation for Locally Differentially Private Protocols
milestones.note: Revisits and improves EM-based estimation methods for local differential privacy protocols to yield more reasonable results.

milestones.note: Improves differentially private data stream release by allowing delay rather than requiring real-time output.

sp.narrative:
Differential privacy at IEEE S&P spans both the theory of privacy mechanisms and their application to machine learning. The 2018-2019 cohort tackled local DP for data collection: Locally Differentially Private Frequent Itemset Mining (S&P 2018) addressed federated frequency estimation under local DP, while PrivKV: Key-Value Data Collection with Local Differential Privacy (S&P 2019) extended local DP to richer structured data types.

The 2019 wave then connected DP directly to ML robustness. Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy (S&P 2019) showed that randomized smoothing with DP mechanisms yields provable adversarial robustness certificates. Differentially Private Model Publishing for Deep Learning (S&P 2019) and Towards Practical Differentially Private Convex Optimization (S&P 2019) worked to close the accuracy gap between DP-trained and non-private models.

From 2020-2021, papers both strengthened the theory and attacked deployed systems. SoK: Differential Privacy as a Causal Property (S&P 2020) reframed DP in causal terms, clarifying what the guarantee actually means. DP-Sniper: Black-Box Discovery of Differential Privacy Violations using Classifiers (S&P 2021) turned ML into a tool for finding DP implementation bugs. Manipulation Attacks in Local Differential Privacy (S&P 2021) showed that local DP protocols are vulnerable to poisoning by malicious participants.

By 2022-2024, Are We There Yet? Timing and Floating-Point Attacks on Differential Privacy Systems (S&P 2022) found that floating-point non-determinism and timing channels can violate DP guarantees in real implementations. SoK: Privacy-Preserving Data Synthesis (S&P 2024) synthesized synthetic-data generation under DP as a practical privacy mechanism.

uss.narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this list grappled with two practical realities of differential privacy (DP): how well it actually protects machine learning, and how local DP behaves once it leaves the textbook. "Evaluating Differentially Private Machine Learning in Practice" (USENIX 2019) sounded an early, widely-cited warning that the privacy budget epsilon is often set so loosely that real guarantees evaporate, while "When the Signal is in the Noise: Exploiting Diffix's Sticky Noise" (USENIX 2019) attacked a deployed anonymization system to show how fragile non-rigorous schemes are. In parallel, the local DP (LDP) thread began maturing toward utility: "Utility-Optimized Local Differential Privacy Mechanisms for Distribution Estimation" (USENIX 2019) and "PCKV" (USENIX 2020) pushed LDP beyond simple homogeneous frequency estimation toward correlated key-value and sensitivity-aware data.

The early 2020s broadened DP from a theoretical tool into a systems and deployment problem. Several papers married DP with cryptography and distributed settings: "Secure Multi-party Computation of Differentially Private Median" (USENIX 2020), "How to Make Private Distributed Cardinality Estimation Practical, and Get Differential Privacy for Free" (USENIX 2021), and "Batched Differentially Private Information Retrieval" (USENIX 2022) all showed DP composing with secure computation. Application breadth also exploded, from software telemetry in "Differentially-Private Control-Flow Node Coverage for Software Usage Analysis" (USENIX 2020), to eye-tracking in "Kalεido" (USENIX 2021), to synthetic data and graphs in "PrivSyn" (USENIX 2021) and "Locally Differentially Private Analysis of Graph Statistics" (USENIX 2021). Crucially, this period also exposed LDP's attack surface: "Data Poisoning Attacks to Local Differential Privacy Protocols" (USENIX 2021) showed that the same untrusted-aggregator model that protects users lets malicious users skew results.

By the mid-2020s the field turned reflective and human-facing. "What Are the Chances? Explaining the Epsilon Parameter in Differential Privacy" (USENIX 2023) tackled the usability gap the 2019 evaluation paper foreshadowed, asking how to communicate epsilon to real people, while DP moved deep into modern ML with "PrivateFL" (USENIX 2023) for federated learning, "PrivGraph" (USENIX 2023) for graph publication, and generative methods like "dp-promise: Differentially Private Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Image Synthesis" (USENIX 2024).

The current frontier, dominated by USENIX 2024-2025, splits in two directions. One is rigorous privacy auditing and tighter accounting: "Efficient Privacy Auditing in Federated Learning" (USENIX 2024), "Closed-Form Bounds for DP-SGD against Record-level Inference" (USENIX 2024), "Privacy Audit as Bits Transmission: (Im)possibilities for Audit by One Run" (USENIX 2025), and "General-Purpose f-DP Estimation and Auditing in a Black-Box Setting" (USENIX 2025) push toward empirically and formally verifying claimed guarantees. The other is scaling DP to large modern models and refining LDP utility, seen in "Unlocking the Power of Differentially Private Zeroth-order Optimization for Fine-tuning LLMs" (USENIX 2025), "Addressing Sensitivity Distinction in Local Differential Privacy" (USENIX 2025), and the reality check "SoK: Can Synthetic Images Replace Real Data?" (USENIX 2025). The arc runs from questioning whether DP delivers in practice, through broad deployment, to a mature insistence on auditing what was deployed.

top4.narrative:
The earliest papers in this list, all from 2018, mark differential privacy's transition from theory to deployable systems and tooling. On the local DP (LDP) side, where users perturb their own data before sending it to an untrusted collector, "Locally Differentially Private Frequent Itemset Mining" (S&P 2018) and "CALM: Consistent Adaptive Local Marginal for Marginal Release under Local Differential Privacy" (CCS 2018) pushed LDP beyond simple frequency estimation toward richer analytics like itemsets and marginals. In parallel, a verification thread emerged: "Detecting Violations of Differential Privacy" (CCS 2018) and "DP-Finder" (CCS 2018) attacked the problem that the sophisticated mechanisms being published were often buggy, building tools to find privacy violations automatically.

Around 2019, the center of gravity shifted toward machine learning. "Evaluating Differentially Private Machine Learning in Practice" (USENIX 2019) became a touchstone by showing how loosely the privacy budget epsilon was being interpreted, while "Differentially Private Model Publishing for Deep Learning" (S&P 2019) and "Towards Practical Differentially Private Convex Optimization" (S&P 2019) worked on making private training usable. A striking cross-over result, "Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy" (S&P 2019), repurposed DP machinery for adversarial robustness rather than privacy itself. LDP analytics kept maturing too, with "PrivKV" (S&P 2019) extending collection to key-value data.

The 2020-2021 period brought two complementary maturations: scaling the theory and stress-testing the guarantees. The shuffle model emerged as a middle ground between local and central DP, studied in "Private Summation in the Multi-Message Shuffle Model" (CCS 2020) and "On the Rényi Differential Privacy of the Shuffle Model" (CCS 2021). At the same time, an adversarial-auditing line questioned whether deployed DP actually delivered: "Adversary Instantiation: Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Machine Learning" (S&P 2021) empirically probed DP-SGD's real leakage, "Manipulation Attacks in Local Differential Privacy" (S&P 2021) showed malicious users could skew LDP aggregates, and "DP-Sniper" (S&P 2021) automated black-box discovery of violations. A human-factors thread also opened, asking what users actually understand, in "I need a better description: An Investigation Into User Expectations For Differential Privacy" (CCS 2021).

By 2022-2024 the field had become self-critical and application-driven. "Are We There Yet? Timing and Floating-Point Attacks on Differential Privacy Systems" (S&P 2022) showed that even correct math leaks through implementation side channels, continuing the auditing lineage. DP moved into modern ML deployments through "DP-Forward" (CCS 2023) for language models and "PrivateFL" (USENIX 2023) for federated learning, while usability work matured with "What Are the Chances? Explaining the Epsilon Parameter in Differential Privacy" (USENIX 2023). Finally, consolidating SoKs like "SoK: Privacy-Preserving Data Synthesis" (S&P 2024) signal a field that now spans rigorous mechanisms, real-world systems, attacks, and human comprehension.
